title: A reading correction keeps both values and is traceable
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a service advisor, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag). Open the audit trail wherever the build surfaces it for the asset/customer and check entries against the action you just performed.
  2. An asset with a recorded reading you will correct; and a service whose due date moves weeks later when a new reading is entered. Seed the readings on an enrolled meter-driven service.
custom_steps:
1. Correct a reading and open the audit trail; read both the old and the new value.
  2. Enter a new reading that moves a due date weeks out, then trace the moved due date back through the audit trail.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A reading correction keeps both values, each with its timestamp and author.
  • A due date that moved weeks after a new reading is traceable to the reading that moved it.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10576 (S21, The audit trail); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S21; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S21-R4: “A reading correction will keep both values, each with its timestamp and author”
  • S21-E2: “A due date that moved weeks after a new reading must be traceable to the reading that moved it”
